steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.

Combine applesauce, sugar, oil, eggs, and milk in a large bowl; beat well. Sift in flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt; stir until smooth. Fold in pecans. Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the loaf comes out clean, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Spiced Applesauce Bread
raw_recipe.description: This moist applesauce bread is an easy-to-make quick bread with chopped pecans and warm fall spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice.
raw_recipe.name: Spiced Applesauce Bread

review.reviewBody: I have to give this bread a four star rating as written, but by incorporating some different reviewers suggestions, this bread is definitiely a 5+!! First of all, I used 1 1/2 cups of chunky applesauce and only 1/4 cup of oil. I also used 1/2 cup of white sugar and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. I doubled all the spices- this was definitely a must for me. I didn't think the bread was even that spicy like that, especially for a recipe called SPICED Applesauce Bread. I added a crumb topping of 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup chopped pecans and 1/2 tsp. cinnamon as well. This turned this bread into a real treat! I loved how moist the bread was, and it made my house smell amazing while it baked. I'm definitely not a baker (cooking is much more my cup of tea), so if I can make an amazing applesauce bread with this recipe, anybody can!

It is delicious!
I did make a few changes. I knew I would like a bit more spice, so I increased cinnamon to 1 tsp. I didn't have allspice, so I used 1/8 tsp clove. Added 1/2 cup chocolate chips and 1/4 cup raisins.
And, I reduced the sugar to 3/4 cup... it is still a sweet loaf.

I used 3 small loaf pans, 4"x3" and baked for 30 minutes in a convection toaster oven.

Saving this recipe.

After reading reviews, I decided to make the follow alterations: Used 1/2c unbleached AP flour, and 1/2c whole wheat flour. Used apple cider instead of milk, and decreased the oil to 1/4c . I increased the baking powder, cinnamon and allspice to 1 tsp., and increase the freshly ground nutmeg to 1/4 tsp. I added 1 chopped granny smith apple and about 1/2c of chopped walnuts. I baked mine in small loaf pans for gifts. Wonderful!

I found this recipe in a Southern Living cookbook except the books version calls for 1/2 C pecans, 1/4C light brown sugar and 1/2 Tsp cinnamon to be sprinkled over the batter. I think this addition would turn a lot of the low star reviews into higher ratings. You get extra sweetness and spice with this addition.

It was for thanksgiving so I substituted 1-14oz can Ocean Spray whole berry cranberry sauce in exchange for the applesauce. I also added an extra tablespoon of milk as the cranberry sauce is a gelatin instead of semi liquid like applesauce. Finally I spread extra pecans on the top. Took 1:35 in my over checking every 10 minutes after 45. Totally worth it. It was cold and windy here so oven may have been a little cool,

Yummmm! Read through some other reviews and made tweaks that sounded good (along with limitations to ingredients on hand). I altered to have: 1 c applesauce and half cup of minced apple, sanded the greased pan with sugar, used almond milk vanilla creamer instead of milk, did half brown sugar and half sugar (and I'll increase sugar by another 1/4 cup next time), added a streusel topping, used walnuts instead of pecans, and went nuts with the spices)! I suggest to at least double the cinnamon, allspice and nutmeg, and add similar amounts of clove, cardamom, orange peel, and pumpkin pie spice - and then just a dash of cayenne for some je ne sais quoi. So freaking GOOD! Baked up perfectly in exactly one hour for me: nice, dense and moist after a wooden kebab stick came out clean testing for doneness (which I use instead of toothpicks because they're longer).

This is a wonderful base recipe - loads of room for creativity to make it your own!

Great recipe. I changed a few things. Skipped the oil and added more applesauce. I also added cardamom, went heavy on the cinnamon and I used less than half a cup of evaporated cane juice sugar. I wanted them to be flavorful but not to be too sweet because I intend to eat them for breakfast with my homemade vegan butter. Very delicious! Very moist! I made 18 cupcakes and I baked them for about 25-30 min just keep an eye open for them. They were very moist and not dense. Very cakey! The batter was wet and thick and it caused my cupcake liners to get stuck so be careful! I had to stick the cupcakes upside down inside the microwave, on a plate and then I had to moistened a paper towel and placed it on top of them and microwave for 15 sec to be able to remove the liner.

I made this several times. I started adding chopped, dried cranberries and chocolate chips. I use 50/50 brown sugar and white sugar. I also use a brown sugar streusel topping. This recipe makes good muffins and even better mini muffins. Regular muffins took about 20-23 minutes, mini muffins about 15-18 minutes. The bread style I had to extend the cooking time by 10-15 minutes as the very center was still raw. My family swears it's one of the best things they've eaten. I didn't try using butter instead of oil as it tastes so good as is.

My husband and I enjoyed this bread, but the batter ran over the sides of the pan. So use a slightly bigger bread pan than listed in the recipe. I also deleted the nuts in favor of raisins. We found letting the bread set for a day made it more moist. Maybe it was the raisin addition. I'll make this again for sure.

Great base recipe I also added oil and butter to make super moist two cups of applesauce also one banana some cocoa powder three times the spices I folded in some oatmeal produced two loaf pans of moist spiced sweet dessert my family all loved

I decided to give this 5 stars still despite all the changes I made because if there’s anyone else looking for a similar recipe like I was, the original recipe serves as a really good base.

I read all the reviews and doubled my spices. I also don’t like all spice so instead I used 1/4 ground cardamom & 1/4 ginger. I also used Pamela’s GF flour instead of regular flour. I used ghee and butter in place of the oil. I subbed maple syrup the white sugar. I *didn’t* use any milk. Lastly, I made my own applesauce following ‘Sarah’s Applesauce Recipe’, which can also be found on this site. It made exactly enough for this spiced bread cake.

Despite GF flour being so dry and despite not using any milk, this was still a very wet batter and took much longer to cook. But it smelled heavenly and tastes heavenly. It’s moist, has a really wonderful dense-yet-airy texture, and the flavor is fantastic. Really loving the cinnamon-nutmeg-cardamom-ginger combo.
Good to try.
Delicious. I did them as muffins and added a little butter, brown sugar, and fresh pineapple to the bottom of the tin.
Well, I went to make this recipe, and I couldn't find my nutmeg and allspice. So, I substituted with a tablespoon of pumpkin spice, and doubled the cinnamon. It was moist and delicious!
I made this with quince instead of apple sauce, added chocolate chips, and doubled the spices…really easy and excellent!
This is my boyfriend’s favorite recipe! He’s unsure about baked goods and desserts, but this is the first one where I’ve caught him sneaking seconds! :D
We enjoyed it. Great with tea/coffee.
Added raisins.
Made 2 loaves
We love this bread. I read a couple of other reviews and followed the suggestion to add extra apple sauce. I used my canned apple-pear sauce and added the extra half cup as apple butter.
